svg.title: TOPAK H1 — The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them
svg.desc: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins what it follows.

text.tspan: The corpus: layers, precedence, and how a change moves through them

svg.text: TOPAK is a design corpus in its genesis phase. The checkpoint is the state of record and wins over the narrative; records are immutable after ratification except by typed History rows; the narrative and the glossary are cut with each checkpoint; derived analyses are dated and frozen; specifications, the floor, the reference and the rehearsal are evidence; manifests measure every cut at the commit it measured, and the reference pins

text.tspan: 1 · Precedence: who wins, who explains, who is evidence, who measures

svg.text: Current: Genesis Checkpoint G11 (2026.10.09, tag G11). Each checkpoint is one cut, never revised: what each record says, what was ratified and by whom, what is owed, what is open, and the manifest that measures it. G11 is the first whose trusted base names two deductive methods, and the first to record a known defect in a trust root kept in use (ADR-0053; ADR-0046 A2).

Where the narrative and the checkpoint disagree, the checkpoint wins. G11 names ToO revision 14 as standing, not revised at G11, and behind it on Lean, the prover's cases, liveness and the workflow records (items 14, 100); revision 15 is cut against G11 afterwards.
checkpoints/README.md names G11 and holds the 2026.09.30 layout map, the one place stale paths resolve.
ADR-0001 onward, one file each, numbered in the order settled; 54 files to ADR-0055, ADR-0014 reserved. Twelve amendments are pending, every
Never edited after ratification except by a typed History row: an amendment, an erratum, a revision before ratification, a dependent entry, or a
Provisional since Batch 34: ratified, in force, subject to redesign, saying what it lacked (ADR-0029 A4): ADR-0050, ADR-0052 and four amendments
decisions/README.md gives status at G11 and is a convenience; the checkpoint is the state of record.
theory-of-operation.md, the head: revision 15 (2026.10.09, tag ToO-rev15), cut against G11; revision 14, against G10, stands at G11 and is what
G11's manifest measures. A revision is an edit, a Changes appendix, a commit and a tag.
glossary.md, revised in place and tagged glossary-<date>; 2026.10.09 against G11.
architecture-description.md: a draft, revision 3 against G11, untagged; an arc42 index over the records that decides nothing. G10 measures
revisions/: a closed archive of the dated revisions before the cut (09.10 to rev 9).
One-shot analyses, reviews and assessments. A derived document is never revised; a new one is written. 32 files in G11's manifest, three added
Ten accepted records cite files here by path in their provenance notes, so names do not change.
The 09.17 and 09.26 glossaries stay here, frozen, because records cite them.

The first cut of all is the v1 corpus manifest (2026.09.15). Until G1 the Theory of Operation carried the
state of record itself: G1 superseded manifest v1 in full and, as state of record, the 09.15 ToO rev 4's
ledger, ADR log, open list, genesis plan and next steps; rev 4 stayed in force as narrative (G1 header).
made as an edit; cut from G7
Narrative revisions (violet): the nine dated files before the cut sit in narrative/revisions/, byte-identical moves, six of them from before git; revisions 7 to 15 are tagged ToO-rev7 … ToO-rev15.

text.tspan: 3 · How a change moves through the corpus

svg.text: A record is drafted and revised in place while Proposed: History rows
R1, R2 …, each "Applied — Proposed record, revised in place".
The genesis custodian ratifies under ADR-0029 §2, in numbered
batches (G9: Batch 26; G10: Batches 27–35, on two days; G11: 36 and
Accepted (genesis); a confirmation-required marker C1–C4 when the
first post-bootstrap quorum must review it (ADR-0029 §4); provisional
when it did not meet its own ratification condition and says what it
Only typed History rows: an amendment (A1 …), an erratum (E1 …),
or a dependent entry (B22 …) when another record's ratification
A dependent amendment is drafted to be applied as marked, beside
the text it changes (G10 §5); twelve are pending at G11, all on
Proposed records. A pending amendment may be withdrawn
Gn supersedes Gn−1 as the state of record: ratifications, ledger, open
list. tools/cut-manifest.sh cuts SHA256SUMS-Gn under EXCLUDE;
index.tsv gains a row naming the commit; a tag Gn.
The ToO is edited against the checkpoint, with a "Changes from
revision N" appendix, a commit and a tag ToO-revN; the glossary is
revised in place. Until then the checkpoint wins (G11 item 100 owes rev
mechanism/corpus-pins.sha256: the drift test fails when a pinned
record moves; review, bring the code into line or register the
divergence, then replace the pin line.
An ADR-0033 addendum cites the new SHA256SUMS-REF-<date>.

Example, G10 (2026.10.04–05): ADR-0005 ratified alone in Batch 27 (44ff854) → Batches 28 to 31, among them ADR-0033 A7 ratified ahead of ADR-0036 and the Run profile (9b3cecd, efd83b9) → the reference rebuilt in five stages to records then Proposed, each with an ADR-0033 addendum and a manifest, SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.05 to -05e (7764e52, c15026d, c7de2ba, 9c57221, 7d8c7db); A9 accepted alone in Batch 32 → Batch 33, the race (65185ed) → Batch

34, five records, two provisional, and twenty-six dependent amendments applied as marked (075b2e7) → Batch 35 (e4b174e) → G10 cut, SHA256SUMS-G10, 499 entries (029a31b) → ToO revision 14, the glossary, the architecture description's revision 2, the reviewer's guide and G10's index row (bd26b97). SHA256SUMS-G9 fails at G10's tree, by construction. G11 (2026.10.06–09): ADR-0053 alone in Batch 36 (15ae7f1) → the prover's two unsound cases in Batch 37 (848aed5)

→ two Proposed records built at the reference, SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.08 and -09 → G11 cut, 604 entries (ce8f460) → its index row → ToO revision 15, the glossary, the architecture description's revision 3 and the reviewer's guide (a77d226).

text.tspan: Two kinds of manifest failure that are correct

svg.text: SHA256SUMS-G10 fails at G11's tree by construction (fifteen accepted records changed, with the narrative and the binding table) and verifies 499 of 499 at 029a31b (G11 §9).

SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.09 fails two entries at G11's tree, the pin file and the register, which moved after 749d54f; 116 of 116 there. -10.08 fails three, workflow.rs among them, and verifies whole at its own commit.
Frozen records that cite pre-move paths are not edited: their digests are pinned. Two such citations are knowingly left stale and resolve through the layout map.

text.tspan: Pointers still behind the state of record

svg.text: G11's header names revision 14 as the standing narrative; revision 15 is written against G11 afterwards (items 14, 100). The tags item 100 owed, G11, REF-2026.10.08 and -09, ToO-rev15 and glossary-2026.10.09, are made.

The floor stages open with a comment that is wrong, "not what the reference follows" (G11 item 91); floor/README.md says the reference links the labels stage, where it links workflow (G11 §2.2), and that T_persona is not yet read,
where it is (ADR-0033 A6); two policy comments call ADR-0049 Proposed (item 98).
decisions/README.md gives status at G11 under a column still headed "Status at G8". REVIEWERS_GUIDE_README.md is kept current outside the manifest (item 99).
